note: The note kinds a Notes paragraph's leading label maps to. Read by BOTH static/note-blocks.js (display grouping) and import_cleanup (the data rule), so the two cannot disagree about what a label means. corpus_* are measured over the 177 recipe_notes rows, re-read on 2026-10-05. A kind with 0 is carried for imports, not for this corpus.
restates_the_kind: Per kind, the labels that merely RESTATE it. The page groups by kind and prints the kind's header over the group, so a note opening "Note:" under a heading reading "Notes" says it twice and the label comes off. A label NOT on this list says more than the header does and becomes the note's title instead: "To Store" and "To Freeze" are both the storage kind and are the pair a title exists to tell apart. THIS IS A LIST AND NOT A GRAMMAR RULE. An earlier version compared the label against the kind name with a plural rule, which titled "Storing" on the grounds that it is not spelled "Storage". Andy's call, 2026-10-08: "Storing" restates Storage and "Reminder" does not restate Notes. A label on no list is a judgement about words, so it is written down rather than derived.
